# NexGenio LTD
> Boutique GRC and security architecture consultancy based in Malta, helping organisations across Europe navigate NIS2, DORA, ISO 27001/42001/22301, and AI governance requirements.

## Pages

- [Home](https://nexgenio.com/) — ISO & regulatory compliance programmes for essential entities, financial entities, and organisations across Europe
- [Training Hub](https://nexgenio.com/training/index.html) — All PECB-certified training courses (self-paced and live), with exam and certificate included

## Reference Tables

- [NIS2 framework mapping](https://nexgenio.com/nis2-iso-27001-mapping.html) — All 49 requirements of the Annex to Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 mapped to eleven frameworks. Nine are reproduced from ENISA's own mapping table version 1.1 (10 July 2025): ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clauses and Annex A controls, NIST CSF 2.0, ETSI EN 319 401, CEN/TS 18026, and the national frameworks of Belgium (CyberFundamentals), Finland (Kybermittari), Greece (Ministerial Decision 1689/2025), Spain (ENS) and France. Two further columns are NexGenio original work because no regulator or standards body has published either: the ISA/IEC 62443 series for operational technology, mapped at requirement-family level across 62443-2-1:2024, -3-3, -3-2 and -4-1, and ISO 22301:2019 for business continuity, mapped at clause level. The 22301 column exists because ENISA correlates NIS2 Article 21(2)(c) to no continuity standard at all, leaving section 4 resting on three ISO 27001 controls. Also includes a reverse index from each of the 93 Annex A controls to the NIS2 requirements it serves, the Article 21(2) linkage for every requirement, and a list of the NIS2 obligations that have no ISO 27001 equivalent — registration with the national authority, the 24-hour/72-hour/one-month incident reporting cascade, and the Article 20 management body accountability and training duty. 69 of the 93 Annex A controls are referenced by the mapping. Free, no signup

- [DORA framework mapping](https://nexgenio.com/dora-mapping.html) — All 41 substantive articles of Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774, the DORA regulatory technical standard on ICT risk management, mapped to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (clauses and Annex A controls), ISO 22301:2019 (clause level) and PCI DSS v4.0.1 (12 requirements). Unlike the NIS2 mapping, this is entirely NexGenio original work: no European Supervisory Authority, ENISA, national competent authority, ISO, NIST or PCI SSC has published a DORA crosswalk, and the frequently repeated claim that the RTS was drafted in alignment with ISO 27001 appears nowhere in the regulation, the consultation paper (JC 2023 39) or the final report (JC 2023 86). The page's central argument is that criticality is the hinge of the whole regulation and is a measurement rather than a label: 22 of the 41 articles condition their obligation on something being critical or important — a flag computed from the regulation's own wording and shown on each article — and the RTS sets out no method for determining it. The instrument that does is a business impact analysis, ISO 22301:2019 clause 8.2, which reasons from consequence over time and is indifferent to cause, unlike an information security risk assessment reasoning from threat and likelihood. Consequence is measured against the business itself, so criticality is derived downward from business risk rather than upward from the technology estate; Article 28(2)(a) makes the management body responsible for the framework serving the business strategy and risk appetite and Article 28(2)(d) requires that same body to approve the business impact analysis. The acquisition and third-party articles therefore carry ISO 22301 clauses, because Article 4(2)(b) requires recovery time and recovery point objectives to sit in the ICT asset record alongside the third-party provider's support end dates, Article 16(2) requires acquisition testing commensurate to criticality and for central securities depositories requires it to involve the interdependencies identified in their business continuity policy, and Article 37(a) requires non-functional requirements approved before acquisition. A recovery objective that is not in the contract is an aspiration. The page's distinctive feature is that it shows both regimes side by side with a regime filter — the full ICT risk management framework under DORA Article 15 (Title II, Articles 2 to 27) and the simplified framework under DORA Article 16 (Title III, Articles 28 to 41) — and derives the correspondence between them from the regulation's own structure. Seven Title III articles each compress several full-framework articles, Article 35 absorbing six of them, and three Title II articles have no Title III counterpart at all: Article 19 on human resources policy, Article 22 on the ICT-related incident management policy and Article 23 on anomalous activity detection. The page states explicitly that silence in Title III is not an exemption, because DORA Articles 17 to 23 on incident classification and reporting and Article 5(2) on management body accountability apply regardless of regime. Also lists the DORA duties no management system standard produces — the register of information, the major incident reporting cascade, the mandatory contractual terms, threat-led penetration testing and management body accountability. Publishes no coverage percentage, by design. Free, no signup

## Regulatory Services

- [NIS2 compliance](https://nexgenio.com/nis2.html) — Scope determination for essential and important entities, the ten Article 21 risk management measures, Article 20 board accountability, incident reporting timelines and supply chain security. Covers the Dutch Cyberbeveiligingswet, in force 15 August 2026. Entry point is the fixed-scope, fixed-price NIS2 Baseline Check
- [DORA Article 16](https://nexgenio.com/dora-article-16.html) — The simplified ICT risk management framework for smaller financial entities: the six categories it covers, the four obligations that fall away, and why eligibility cannot be read off a public register. Relevant to small and non-interconnected investment firms, exempted payment and e-money institutions, small IORPs and microenterprises
- [NIS2 board training](https://nexgenio.com/nis2-board-training.html) — Management body training meeting the NIS2 Article 20(2) duty. Half-day board sessions, annual refreshers and new director onboarding, in English or German, with an evidence pack of agenda, materials and attendance record
